text: At last his son, the new chief of the tribe, came to him and asked, Is it well with you. <break time="0.8s" /> It is well, the old man answered, and his son told him that there was wood beside him and that the fire burned bright. <break time="0.8s" /> The son said that the morning was gray and the cold had broken, and that it would snow before long. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, even now it is snowing, Koskoosh agreed, and the son explained that the tribe was hurrying because their bundles were heavy. <break time="0.8s" /> He added that their stomachs were empty and the trail was long, and then he asked once more if all was well. <break time="0.8s" /> It is well, said Koskoosh, for I am like last years leaf, hanging lightly on its stem, and I will fall at the first breath of wind. <break time="0.8s" /> My eyes no longer show me the way, my feet are heavy, and I am tired, he went on. <break time="0.8s" /> The son went away, and Koskoosh listened until the sound of his snowshoes faded and he knew that his son was gone forever. <break time="0.8s" /> It was then that he reached out and touched the small pile of wood that Sit cum to ha had gathered for him. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought that if she had cared more about her grandfather than about the trail, she would have gathered more.
